title: Post-SOW Readiness & Baseline Survey
lede: Fielded after signature and before kickoff. Two jobs, and they are different: establish whether this organization can execute what it signed, and capture the numbers that every later claim of improvement will be measured against. Get the second one wrong and the optimization program has nothing to stand on.

questions.text: Full name
Job title and department
What is your authority on this project?
How much of your time is allocated to this project?
questions.logic: "Nothing formally allocated" on the project owner is the most common root cause of a slipped go-live, and it is visible before kickoff if anyone asks.

questions.text: Who is your named backup if you are unavailable for two weeks?
Were you involved before signature?
questions.logic: Someone who inherited the project has no memory of what was promised. Where this is "no", budget time to re-establish scope rather than assuming it.

questions.text: Is there an executive sponsor who is visibly engaged?
How are decisions made on this project?
What is the longest a decision has taken to get made so far?
questions.logic: The best available predictor of how long the next decision will take. It is not a judgment; it is a planning input and belongs in the schedule.

questions.text: Is there a change-control process this project must follow?
Has the business case been communicated beyond the project team?
options: There is no written business case

questions.text: Has AI handling or analysing customer conversations been approved internally?
questions.logic: Confirms the pre-SOW P6.3 answer after signature. A module that was quoted as phase 1 against a verbal approval is a module at risk.

questions.text: Is there a works council, union or employee-representation step required?
questions.logic: Recording, quality management and workforce management frequently require consultation. "Not yet engaged" is a schedule dependency, not a formality.

questions.text: What has to be true internally for this project to be considered a success?
Has the RingCentral account been provisioned?
Who holds super-admin on the RingCentral account?
questions.logic: A shared or absent super-admin is a day-one governance finding. It also makes every subsequent access question ambiguous.

questions.text: Has an API or integration application been created for reporting access?
questions.logic: The optimization program reads RingCentral through a JWT-authenticated application with read-only scopes. Creating it is a customer action with a lead time, and it blocks the first baseline run.

questions.text: Which scopes have been granted to that application?
questions.logic: Scope changes take a short time to propagate. A failed first run is usually propagation lag, not a permissions error — re-check before escalating.

questions.text: Is there a RingCX account, and is it a parent or sub-account?
questions.logic: RingCX permissions are granted per account. A role held on a sub-account does not operate on the parent, and that distinction has produced more false "permission denied" diagnoses than any other RingCX fact.

questions.text: Are RingSense (AI Conversation Expert) licences assigned?
Is WEM (Workforce Engagement Management) licensed on RingCX?
questions.logic: Without WEM, RingCX queue statistics are available same-day only. Historical queue reporting across a window requires it, and a baseline that assumes otherwise cannot be produced.

questions.text: Has a technical contact been named to RingCentral support?
Current telephony platform and version
Current contact-centre platform, if separate
Has the network been assessed for voice?
questions.logic: Voice quality findings that appear at the first optimization review are almost always network findings that nobody looked for before go-live.

questions.text: Which of these are in place?
Which systems must RingCentral connect to?
Is Microsoft Teams in use for calling?
What is the identity provider?
Is SCIM provisioning available from that identity provider?
How are devices currently managed?
Describe anything custom that touches telephony today.
Who owns telephony day to day?
Who owns the contact centre day to day?
Who owns reporting and analytics?
Who owns identity and access?
Who owns network?
Are any of those roles vacant or shared with someone who has another full-time job?
questions.logic: Coverage gaps are the most reliable predictor of a stalled day-2. They are also the easiest thing to plan around if named before kickoff.

questions.text: Is there a named owner for the optimization program after go-live?
questions.logic: A program with no day-2 owner produces findings nobody actions. O3.1 measures the consequence six months later.

questions.text: Which groups need to be consulted before changes go live?
What does good look like twelve months after go-live?
Is this primarily a cost project, an experience project or a capability project?
What is the one thing that must not get worse?
questions.logic: Often more useful than the success criteria. It names the thing that will get escalated if it slips.

questions.text: How much process change is the organization prepared to absorb?
Will routing be rebuilt as-is or redesigned?
Is there an appetite to retire anything as part of this?
What would make the front line say this was an improvement?
Which capabilities do you believe are in scope, and when?
questions.logic: Do not pre-fill this from the pre-SOW P6.1. It is asked blind on purpose. The delta between what was asked for before signature and what is believed afterwards is the only measurable trust signal available at kickoff, and pre-filling destroys it.

questions.text: Is there a plan for training end users?
Who will deliver training?
How have previous platform changes been communicated?
Is there a champion network or super-user group?
Who handles day-2 support?
Will the service desk be trained before go-live?
questions.logic: An untrained service desk at cutover converts every user question into an escalation, and the volume is highest in exactly the week when attention is scarcest.

questions.text: Is there a plan to measure adoption after go-live?
What would stop someone using the new platform and carrying on as before?
Target go-live date
Is that date fixed or indicative?
Can the migration be phased?
Which complexity factors apply?
Is there a period when change is not permitted?
What is the rollback plan if cutover fails?
What is the biggest risk to this project, in your view?
Have porting documents (CSRs) been supplied in full?
questions.logic: Porting timelines start here. This is the most common cause of a go-live date moving, and it is entirely within the customer's control.

questions.text: Do you have access to historical reporting from your current platform?
options: No, the incumbent vendor must pull it
questions.logic: "No" or "Unknown" triggers an immediate action item: request the export before the incumbent contract lapses. Historical data is routinely lost at cutover and cannot be recovered afterwards.

questions.text: Which period are you reporting on?
questions.logic: RingCentral Business Analytics serves 184 days. A trailing-12-month baseline cannot be reproduced from RingCentral later, so it must come from the incumbent platform and be labelled as such for the life of the engagement.

questions.text: Is that period representative of normal volume?
Where will you share the underlying reports or exports? Provide a link or name the person sending them.
Which sections are you personally able to answer? Anything you cannot, name a delegate in the next field.
questions.logic: Makes delegation explicit instead of producing guessed answers. Anything unselected becomes a named follow-up rather than a silent gap.

questions.text: Name a delegate for any section you did not select.
Is anyone currently producing a regular report on these numbers?
questions.logic: An organization with no existing reporting habit will not acquire one at go-live. Where the answer is "no", the optimization program is the reporting function, and that should be said out loud rather than assumed.

questions.text: Inbound calls per month: ____  ·  Outbound calls per month: ____  ·  Internal extensions: ____  ·  Assigned DIDs: ____
Call queues in production: ____  ·  IVR menus or auto-receptionists: ____  ·  Voicemail boxes: ____  ·  Shared lines or delegation pairs: ____
Peak concurrent calls: ____  ·  Analog or fax endpoints: ____  ·  SMS/MMS messages per month: ____
Call-queue answer performance today:
If measured — queue average speed to answer (sec): ____  ·  Missed or overflowed queue calls per month: ____  ·  Voicemails left per month: ____
blanks: If measured — queue average speed to answer (sec)
Missed or overflowed queue calls per month

questions.text: DIDs to port: ____  ·  Toll-free numbers: ____  ·  Carriers involved: ____
Voice-quality complaints per month:
Call-recording retention requirement, in months, and what drives it.
Source of the numbers above:
questions.logic: "Mix of both" is a provenance answer, not a quality one. Analytics and Call Log count different things and will not reconcile; a blended figure cannot be reproduced and is reported as an estimate.

questions.text: How many sites have a defined emergency location today?
questions.logic: Carries straight into the layer 0 findings. Emergency-address completeness is not volume-dependent and does not improve on its own.

questions.text: RingEX users: ____  ·  RingCX agent seats: ____  ·  Supervisor seats: ____
Which channels are live today?
Busiest-hour inbound contacts: ____  ·  Daily inbound contacts: ____  ·  Daily outbound contacts: ____
questions.logic: Deliberately re-asked from the pre-SOW P3.4. Do not pre-fill. The delta between the pre-signature belief and the measured figure is a finding in its own right.

questions.text: Where did the numbers in B2.3 come from?
Peak concurrent agents: ____  ·  Peak concurrent contacts: ____
Is contact volume seasonal?
If seasonal — peak month: ____  ·  peak-to-average ratio: ____
Are contact volumes growing, flat or falling?
Service level — Target: ____  ·  Achieved: ____  ·  Threshold used (e.g. 80/20): ____
questions.logic: The threshold is not a detail. A service level quoted without it cannot be compared to anything later.

questions.text: Average speed to answer (sec): ____  ·  Average handle time (sec): ____  ·  After-call work (sec): ____
Abandonment rate: ____  ·  Short-abandon exclusion (sec): ____
First-contact resolution: ____  ·  How measured: ____
questions.logic: FCR measured by a survey, by a repeat-contact window and by supervisor judgment are three different metrics. Without the method, the number means nothing.

questions.text: Transfer rate: ____  ·  Repeat-contact rate: ____  ·  Repeat window used (days): ____
Queues in production: ____  ·  Skills defined: ____  ·  Routing profiles: ____
How is routing configured today?
Is there an overflow or escalation path from every queue?
questions.logic: A queue with no overflow is a queue where calls stop. It is the single most common contact-centre finding and it is invisible until someone looks.

questions.text: Occupancy: ____  ·  Utilization: ____  ·  Shrinkage: ____
Source of the numbers above:
If RingCX is already live — are queue statistics available across a window, or same-day only?
questions.logic: Without WEM, queue statistics come from realTimeData and describe today. A window baseline cannot be built from them, and pretending otherwise produces a number that cannot be reproduced at the first review.

groups.title: RingCX digital channel baseline — email, web chat, SMS, social

questions.text: Email — contacts per month: ____  ·  first-response time: ____  ·  resolution time: ____
Web chat — chats per month: ____  ·  concurrency per agent: ____  ·  average chat duration: ____
SMS — inbound per month: ____  ·  outbound per month: ____  ·  response time: ____
Social — contacts per month: ____  ·  channels covered: ____
Are digital channels handled by the same agents as voice?
Is there a service-level target on digital channels?
Where do digital contacts arrive today?
questions.logic: Digital volume living in a shared mailbox is volume nobody has ever counted. Expect the baseline to be an estimate and label it so.

questions.text: Source of the numbers above:
Is A2P 10DLC brand and campaign registration complete for SMS?
questions.logic: Carrier-controlled and outside anyone's project plan. An unregistered campaign means messages are filtered silently, which presents as "SMS does not work" weeks after go-live.

questions.text: Meetings per month: ____  ·  Participant minutes per month: ____  ·  Active hosts: ____
Is another meeting platform in use?
options: Yes, and it is being retired
questions.logic: Two meeting platforms running in parallel is duplicate spend with a named owner on both sides. It is the clearest cost finding available in layer 7.

questions.text: Meeting rooms with hardware: ____  ·  Rooms to be migrated: ____
Is meeting recording in use?
Is video used as a customer-facing channel?
Source of the numbers above:
Outbound contacts per month: ____  ·  Connect rate: ____  ·  Agents on outbound: ____
What dialing mode is in use?
Dial groups or campaigns in production: ____  ·  Lists loaded per month: ____
blanks: Dial groups or campaigns in production

questions.text: Is there a compliance regime governing outbound?
How are do-not-call lists managed?
questions.logic: A manually managed DNC list is a compliance finding regardless of how well it is maintained, because it cannot be audited.

questions.text: Abandon rate on outbound: ____  ·  Regulatory cap, if any: ____
Source of the numbers above:
Is voice self-service in use today?
Contacts entering self-service per month: ____  ·  Contained without an agent: ____  ·  Containment rate: ____
Intents or flows defined: ____  ·  Intents actively used: ____
How is containment defined today?
options: No transfer and no callback within a window
questions.logic: Containment defined as "no transfer" counts an abandoned caller as a success. Where the definition is not stated, the baseline is not usable.

questions.text: Fallback or escalation rate: ____  ·  Recognition or match rate: ____
Is there a human review loop on self-service outcomes?
Source of the numbers above:

groups.title: RingCX AI agent — chat and digital

questions.text: Is digital self-service in use today?
Digital self-service sessions per month: ____  ·  Contained: ____  ·  Escalated to an agent: ____
Intents defined: ____  ·  Knowledge articles connected: ____
Where does the bot's knowledge come from?
questions.logic: A bot answering from hand-authored content decays the moment the product changes, and nobody notices until containment falls. Where this is the answer, the day-2 plan needs a named content owner.

questions.text: Is the handover to a human seamless, with context carried?
Source of the numbers above:
Is any agent-assist capability in use today?
Is conversation intelligence (RingSense or equivalent) in use?
Calls recorded per month: ____  ·  Calls with insights or transcription: ____  ·  Coverage: ____
What is conversation intelligence used for today?
Has a transcription or AI-analysis consent position been established?
questions.logic: Consent for recording and consent for AI analysis are not the same question, and the second is frequently assumed from the first. Where this is "not addressed", RingSense scope is conditional.

questions.text: Source of the numbers above:
Who produces operational reporting today?
How often is reporting reviewed by the business?
Has a reporting decision ever changed an operational decision?
questions.logic: Distinguishes reporting that exists from reporting that is used. The second is rarer and far more useful to know about.

questions.text: Where does reporting go today?
What happens to historical data at cutover?
questions.logic: "Nothing planned" is an action item with a deadline, not an answer. Once the incumbent contract lapses the data is gone, and every pre-migration comparison goes with it.

questions.text: Is there a data-retention requirement on reporting or recordings?
What question does your current reporting fail to answer?
Is formal quality management in place today?
Evaluations per agent per month: ____  ·  Evaluators: ____  ·  Average QA score: ____
How are calls selected for evaluation?
Is calibration between evaluators performed?
questions.logic: Without calibration, QA scores measure the evaluator rather than the agent, and a QA-score trend over time is not interpretable.

questions.text: Do agents see their own evaluations?
Is coaching tracked to an outcome?
Coverage — calls evaluated as a share of calls handled: ____
blanks: Coverage — calls evaluated as a share of calls handled

questions.text: Source of the numbers above:
Is workforce management in use today?
Forecast accuracy: ____  ·  Schedule adherence: ____  ·  Shrinkage: ____
How far ahead are schedules published?
How are intraday changes handled?
Is there an agreement governing scheduling or adherence?
Is agent availability a known problem today?
Source of the numbers above:
What does an agent use today?
options: A softphone plus a CRM, separately

questions.text: Applications an agent touches in a typical contact: ____
blanks: Applications an agent touches in a typical contact

questions.text: Is screen pop in place?
Is call activity logged to the CRM automatically?
Is a CRM embedded softphone in scope?
Do any agents work from a mobile device?
Are agent desktops managed and standardised?
What takes an agent the longest that should not?

groups.title: Surveys and Voice of the Customer

questions.text: Is a post-contact survey running today?
Survey response rate: ____  ·  CSAT: ____  ·  NPS: ____
How is the survey delivered?
Are survey results linked back to the agent and the contact?
questions.logic: A survey that cannot be traced to a contact is a trend line and nothing more. It cannot support coaching, and it should not be presented as if it could.

questions.text: Is anyone acting on survey results?
Source of the numbers above:
Which regimes apply?
Is payment data ever taken over the phone?
How is recording paused or redacted around sensitive data?
questions.logic: "Not handled" where payment data is taken is a live compliance exposure, and it is a finding on the day it is discovered rather than at the next review.

questions.text: Where must data reside?
Is there a documented retention and deletion policy for recordings?
How are data-subject access requests handled today?
Has security reviewed and approved this platform?
Is SSO enforced for administrative access?
Super-admin accounts today: ____  ·  Accounts with administrative rights: ____
questions.logic: Administrative blast radius, measured. It is a layer 10 finding and one of the few security questions with a defensible number behind it.

questions.text: Answer rate — Baseline: ____  ·  Target: ____  ·  By when: ____
Average speed to answer — Baseline: ____  ·  Target: ____  ·  By when: ____
Abandonment — Baseline: ____  ·  Target: ____  ·  By when: ____
Licence utilisation — Baseline: ____  ·  Target: ____  ·  By when: ____
Self-service containment — Baseline: ____  ·  Target: ____  ·  By when: ____
CSAT or NPS — Baseline: ____  ·  Target: ____  ·  By when: ____
Who agreed these targets?
questions.logic: A target nobody agreed to is a target nobody is measured against. "Sponsor alone" is the most common answer and the most likely to be disowned at the first review.

questions.text: Is the baseline in Part B good enough to measure these targets against?
questions.logic: Asked deliberately after the baseline has been collected. Where the honest answer is "largely estimated", the first optimization review re-baselines rather than reporting movement, and saying so now is far cheaper than discovering it then.

questions.text: How often should the optimization review run?
Who will attend the optimization review from the business?
Is there a budget or mandate to act on findings?
questions.logic: Findings nobody is funded to fix accumulate. O3.1 measures the consequence, and the cause is visible here.

questions.text: Twelve months from now, what single number would make this project unambiguously worth it?
